thread:
incidents-bot: P1 ALERT — multiple model load/warmup failures observed across warmup-pool-3. Errors include GPU OOM during deserialization, repeated container exit code 137, and sporadic NVRTC/compile timeouts. https://runbooks/internal/incident-warmup

oncall-anna: ack, paging now. I’m on it. Will grab logs and check node state.

sre-mike: seeing container exits 137 on gpu-12/gpu-13. dmesg shows oom_killer invoked for process 'redwood-runtime' (RSS spike ~38GB). snippet: `Kernel OOM: killed process 7843 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:8212340kB, anon-rss:39512344kB` :frowning:

ml-eng-jess: fyi, all failing warmups reference model `transformer-xl-v2@v2.14` — we shipped a micro-optimization to fuse attention kernels two days ago (PR #4021). Could be interacting badly with quantized weights.

runtime-lee: also seeing NVRTC timeouts when JITing fused kernels; fallback path triggers heavy CPU deserialization while waiting for kernel compile -> memory spikes. Logs: ```[compile] nvrtc: timeout after 30s, falling back to slower kernel; stack: nvrtc::compile -> fused_attention::build```

support-oliver: customer impact: support ticket #9872 (Acme) and #9879 (Beacon) reporting 5xx for model init endpoints. Both are on dedicated capacity but routed through warmup pool for loads. CSMs notified.

oncall-anna: immediate mitigations I want to try in this order: 1) disable kernel fusion for v2.14 during warmup, 2) increase compile timeout, 3) scale warmup pool, 4) cordon problematic nodes. Will serially roll these.

runtime-lee: patch ready to toggle fusion via model config flag `runtime.fusion=false` and env `REDWOOD_COMPILE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`. Commands: ```kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/warmup-agent REDWOOD_COMPILE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 && kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/warmup-agent``` doing canary.

sre-mike: starting a rolling restart of warmup-agent canary pods (gp2 nodes first). Also cordoning gpu-12 to stop further load: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will watch for flapping.

pm-rina: heads up — engineering to provide a succinct impact blurb for CSMs. Need ETA for mitigation (quick note for customer comms).

ml-eng-jess: quick repro that triggered OOM locally (reduced): ```python
# reproduce warmup spike
model.load(path)
model.compile(fuse_attention=True)
for _ in range(8):
    model.warmup(batch_size=64, seq_len=1024)
``` transient compile+warmup will push memory up.

oncall-anna: Mike — how long to complete the canary restart?

sre-mike: canary done (gp2). warmup success rate jumped from 62% -> 94% on canary. No OOMs during the 10-min window. Proceeding to remaining nodes but pausing before g8 (has other scheduled jobs).

incidents-bot: Severity changed: P1 (Sustained) — multiple customers affected, ongoing mitigation. Link: https://incidents/internal/2429001111

runtime-lee: after disabling fusion and increasing timeout, observed fewer NVRTC fallbacks and a lower peak RSS on warmup pods (~18GB median). Still seeing occasional deserialization errors for one customer on gpu-13.

support-oliver: Acme confirmed partial recovery for their warmup calls; Beacon still seeing intermittent 502s. Tickets updated.

ml-eng-jess: root cause hypothesis: recent fusion optimization increases temporary memory during NVRTC compilation for certain quantized kernels -> spikes during concurrent warmups. Two compounding factors: increased experimental batch_size in prod tests and simultaneous canaries. Recommend reverting the fusion commit for v2.14 and re-run perf tests with controlled batch sizes.

sre-mike: temporarily bumped warmup pool capacity by +2 nodes via autoscaler override: `kubectl -n infra annotate hpa/warmup-pool manual-override=+2` — that buys headroom while we revert.

oncall-anna: handing off to night oncall @sre-mike at 2429001200 — I’ve documented runbook steps, actions taken, and open items. Please monitor warmup success and customer tickets.

pm-rina: CSM note drafted: "We experienced transient model warmup failures impacting initialization for some customers. Engineering has rolled mitigations and most affected customers are recovering. We’ll follow up with postmortem and targeted fixes." :thumbsup:

ml-eng-jess: opened PR #4092 to revert fusion change and added a CI warmup stress test (batch sizes up to 64).

oncall-anna: final checklist for handoff: links to logs, PR, customer ticket ids, and postmortem owner assigned (jess). Leaving channel to oncall. If any regression or new OOMs crop up, escalate immediately.

sre-mike: monitoring, will update on any flaps. :eyes:

support-oliver: closing loop: tickets updated, customers notified, CSMs asked to await final postmortem.

oncall-anna: thanks team — switching to watch mode.
